name: Boston Consulting Group
seo_title: BCG interview process: what to expect
description: What Boston Consulting Group's own careers pages say about applying for consulting roles: the steps, online assessments, case interviews and how to prepare.
intro: This guide sums up what Boston Consulting Group's own careers pages and careers blog say about its consulting interview process, as we checked them on 15 October 2026. Some steps are described only for one country, and we say which. Check BCG's careers site for your office and role before you apply.

items.text: BCG's interview process page lists four steps: an application through its online portal, a skills interview, a case interview and a team interview, with the case and team interviews described for client-facing roles.
A BCG careers blog post by a talent acquisition director says you start on BCG's careers website, create a profile and submit your CV with any other information the role asks for.
The same post says that, depending on the role, the next step may be a phone screen with a recruiter.

For graduate Associate roles in the UK, BCG says you apply online with your CV, may be invited to a short numerical assessment after an initial review, and, if successful, have a final CV review before first-round interviews.
BCG's UK page says all decisions are made after the deadline, so applying later in the window is not a disadvantage.
The UK page says BCG looks for a strong academic record (at least a 2:1 degree or equivalent) and achievements outside your studies.
The UK page recommends applying to no more than three or four offices, and keeping the top two office preferences in your profile consistent with your applications.
BCG London's summer internship is for students in their penultimate year and lasts eight weeks over July and August; the page describes the same application steps as for graduate roles.
BCG's US Associate page says cover letters are not required for its Summer and Full-Time applications, although you may add one.
BCG's global interview process page does not name an online test; the assessments below are described on country pages.
In the UK, BCG describes a short numerical assessment that forms part of your application, but the page does not name the test or describe its format.
BCG's US Associate page says that people who apply through the US application are asked to complete the Consulting Career Assessment (CCA).
According to that page, the CCA invitation arrives 30 to 90 minutes after you apply, the assessment takes about 30 to 35 minutes, and you have 48 hours to finish it.

The US page also says a select group of candidates is invited, about two weeks after the application deadline, to an online case of about 35 minutes, and that anyone who has taken it before is not asked again.
BCG's talent acquisition blog post says AI should never be used without permission during live interviews or digital assessments.

BCG says that in a case interview you get a realistic business problem and work through it step by step: structuring your approach, asking questions, analysing data, doing quick calculations and picking out what matters most.
BCG says there is not always a single right answer, and that what matters most is how you approach the problem and the quality of your reasoning.
BCG's talent acquisition blog post describes the case interview as interactive and close to how BCG case teams work, and says you should see the interviewer as a resource.
The same post says candidates are expected to own their answers, setting the direction and moving the work forward themselves.
It also says case interviews are not meant to be stress tests, but a way to see how you think, structure problems and deal with ambiguity.
The post says interviews for consulting roles include case interviews, and that in many regions or roles there may be more than one interview round; it does not give a number.
A BCG careers blog post by an associate says a typical interview has two parts: a conversation about your background and motivation, then the case itself.
In the UK, BCG says the interview stage includes case-based discussions with senior members of its London consulting team.
BCG describes the skills interview as a traditional interview about your experience, skills and motivation for joining BCG.
BCG's talent acquisition blog post says every role includes a behavioural interview focused on your experiences and achievements.
BCG lists five qualities its consulting interviewers look for: integrity, intellectual curiosity, creative thinking, a collaborative mindset and drive.

BCG's case preparation page gives short lists of dos and don'ts: for example, listen actively, think in a structured way, clarify assumptions and show your thinking, and do not rush, stay silent or interrupt.
BCG offers OneDay@BCG, a set of free virtual job simulations that you can do in your own time, including a strategy consulting module.
The associate's blog post recommends practising cases with other people, as close to a real interview as possible (including time pressure), and with different partners.
BCG says you may use AI tools to help you prepare, for example to brainstorm or organise your thoughts, but not to replace your own voice or to misrepresent your background.
BCG's UK page says it hosts events in September and October, including BCG London case interview preparation sessions with tips from BCG consultants and a live case walkthrough.
BCG's talent acquisition blog post also suggests BCG's webinars and virtual events as a way to learn about the firm.

practice_advice: Practise saying your structure out loud before you start any analysis, so the interviewer can follow your plan.
Do short, timed mental maths drills most days. CaseSpar's drills cover mental maths, chart reading and market sizing.
Run full practice cases from the opening question to a final recommendation, and finish each one with a summary of a minute or less.
Prepare two or three stories from your own experience, each with a clear situation, what you did and the result, and practise telling each in about two minutes.
After every practice case, write down one thing to improve and focus on it in the next one.
